title: Posing the Body
question: How is the friend's body posed, what does a new pose need from the drawing, and which poses come next?
short: Three views, and transforms of them.

The friend is drawn facing us, in profile, or from behind; crawling toward or away from us squashes the front or back view, and lying level turns the profile 90 degrees. Those transforms hold for the poses they were made for, but not for a new angle.
New angles are drawing routines of their own.

Lying along the tent's sleeping bags, the standing friend turned to the bag's slant read as rolling over, and skewed onto it, as too flat. Matthew: "we just need more angles of the body, as their own drawing routine, not cheap 2d transformations". The first one, lying face up along a side wall, is in the game since 0.0.338 (0.0.342 as it stands).
Elbows and knees now turn in three dimensions.

Since 0.0.343 a forearm or a shin can curl toward the front (a knee's toward the back) and swing about the bone above it, and is drawn as it then points: four sliders, on top of every pose and animation.
Layering by depth is the rule to keep.

What is nearer us covers what is farther, part by part: the torso covers the arm behind it, a foot turned behind its leg is drawn under it, a head's hair goes where the head faces away from us. Today one fixed order of layers serves every pose; new poses need their own order.
Next: lying on one side, a three-quarter view, beds along a wall.
Each a routine of its own, plain friend first; costumes and hair styles after (What next, below).
